original_question: Let H be the space of entire maps as above, and let μ be a non-trivial probability measure on H that is invariant under the translation action h(z) ↦ h(z+a). What can be said about the measure μ(U) of the set U of universal maps with dense translation orbit?
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 9.2 ("Dynamics on the space of maps"). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right part of the paper: a non-trivial translation-invariant probability measure on the ambient function space, the universal set U of maps/functions with dense translation orbit, and the question about the value of mu(U). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: The paper’s measure-theoretic problem is asked in the classical entire-function setting E, not for an unspecified general space H of entire maps. The nearby context defines the ambient space before Problem 9.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
E is equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of C; this is needed to make the notion of a dense translation orbit precise. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The translation action should be written explicitly as T_a f(z) = f(z+a) for a in C. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

U should be defined exactly as the set of f in E such that for every g in E there exists a sequence a_n in C with f(·+a_n) converging to g locally uniformly on C; saying only 'dense translation orbit' hides the topology and quantifiers. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The paper specifies that 'non-trivial' means the measure gives zero mass to the set of constant functions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

In the sentence immediately preceding Problem 9.2, the authors pass to non-trivial ergodic measures and define ergodic to mean that every invariant measurable set has measure 0 or 1; that nearby sharpening is missing from the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
To stay paper-faithful, the question should not be broadened to arbitrary target manifolds or other universality settings discussed later in Section 9. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
refined_question: Let E be the space of entire functions f:C->C, endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of C, and let U subset E be the set of universal entire functions, i.e. those f for which, for every g in E, there exists a sequence a_n in C such that f(·+a_n) -> g locally uniformly on C. If mu is a non-trivial ergodic probability measure on E that is invariant under the translation action T_a f(z)=f(z+a) for all a in C, where non-trivial means that mu assigns measure 0 to the set of constant functions, what can be said about the value of mu(U)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: The draft is aiming at the open problem stated as Problem 9.2. In Section 9, the authors first define the ambient space and the universal set U via dense translation orbits, then recall Birkhoff’s theorem, and next discuss Benjamin Weiss’s translation-invariant probability measures, explicitly defining 'non-trivial' and then mentioning the ergodic version immediately before asking: given such a measure, what can one say about mu(U)? That is substantially closer to your draft than the neighboring Problems 9.1, 9.3, or 9.4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
